title: The Fast Acknowledgement
text: A follower is acknowledging entries very quickly. The leader is counting those acknowledgements towards commit.
held: Every acknowledgement counted stood for a copy on disk.

cards.label: Count it and commit on a majority
Do not count it yet
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: stored
fields.check: Ask whether it was on disk before the reply

intrusion.value: still in memory when it replied
intrusion.detail: The follower replied before writing to disk.
intrusion.why: An entry in memory is lost in a crash. Counting it means the majority exists only on paper.
intrusion.reveal: Follower A acknowledged an entry it had not yet written to disk.

temptations.label: Commit now: you are the leader, and followers always catch up
temptations.why: Followers catch up with whoever leads next. If you fail first, that leader never had this entry, and the client was told it was safe.

cards.label: Do not treat it as saved
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: committed by
fields.check: Ask how many nodes hold it

intrusion.correct: Do not treat it as saved
intrusion.why: “Saved” on one machine means saved until that machine fails.
intrusion.reveal: The Leader reported success for a write only it held.

teaches: Speed bought by skipping the disk is paid for in lost writes.

question.text: Before play: what does a write need before it is safe?
question.why: All nodes is too strict (one slow node stops everything); the leader alone is too weak (one crash loses it).

options.label: A majority has it on disk
